issues.legal_issue: Abandoning one statutory ground for eviction does not, without an express amendment, remove part of the leased premises from the eviction petition.
material_facts: The landlord sought possession of the entire leased ground floor on two statutory grounds.
During the revision, the landlord stated that he no longer pressed one ground because his son's business had stopped.
The landlord did not expressly remove the front portion from the premises scheduled in the eviction petition or confine the requested relief to the rest of the premises.
issues.conclusion: The affidavit abandoned one ground for eviction, not the front portion of the premises; the eviction petition continued to concern the entire leased ground floor.
issues.legal_principle: The effect of a pleading or affidavit is determined by a reasonable construction of its terms and the petition as a whole. Where one petition seeks the entire premises on multiple grounds, abandoning one ground does not itself alter the subject matter of the petition; an express deletion or restriction is required.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding and single_petition_covers_entire_premises and landlord_abandons_one_ground and no_express_exclusion_of_part

predicates.eviction_proceeding: A landlord seeks eviction of a tenant from leased premises.
predicates.single_petition_covers_entire_premises: The landlord's single eviction petition seeks possession of the entire leased premises.
predicates.landlord_abandons_one_ground: The landlord states that one legal ground for eviction is no longer pressed.
predicates.no_express_exclusion_of_part: The landlord does not expressly remove any part of the premises from the petition or restrict the relief sought.

issues.definition: When a landlord abandons one ground but does not expressly exclude any part of the premises, the petition continues to cover the entire premises.

issues.legal_issue: Where a statute does not permit partial eviction, a landlord whose bona fide and reasonable need is established for most of the leased premises may obtain possession of the whole premises if the part for which need is not established is insubstantial.
material_facts: The eviction petition concerned the entire leased ground floor, and the landlord had not expressly removed the front portion from it.
The Supreme Court directed the High Court to proceed on the basis that bona fide and reasonable need was established for the ground floor except the front portion.
The statute did not provide for partial eviction, and the comparative-hardship issue had been concluded in the landlord's favour.
The record did not establish whether the front portion was a minor or a substantial part of the ground floor.
issues.conclusion: The High Court had to determine the relative size of the front portion on remand: if it was minor, it was to confirm eviction of the entire ground floor; if it was substantial or major, it was to allow the revision and dismiss the eviction petition.
issues.legal_principle: Where a tenancy cannot be split under the applicable statute, a landlord may have to seek possession of the whole premises even if the bona fide need extends only to part of it. Whether the whole premises may be recovered depends on whether the portion for which need is not established is insubstantial or substantial. The Court relied on Mattulal v. Radhe Lal and referred to Sanyal v. Gian Chand in addressing the bar on splitting the tenancy.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding and no_partial_eviction_authority and bona_fide_need_for_substantial_part and need_not_established_for_remaining_part

predicates.eviction_proceeding: A landlord seeks eviction of a tenant from leased premises.
predicates.no_partial_eviction_authority: The governing law does not authorize an order evicting the tenant from only part of the leased premises.
predicates.bona_fide_need_for_substantial_part: The landlord's bona fide and reasonable need is established for a substantial part of the premises.
predicates.need_not_established_for_remaining_part: The landlord's bona fide and reasonable need is not established for the remaining part of the premises.

issues.definition: If partial eviction is unavailable and need is established for a substantial part but not the rest, the whole-premises eviction outcome depends on whether the part without established need is minor or major.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord occupying part of a building for residential purposes may seek possession for additional residential accommodation of a tenant-occupied part used for non-residential purposes.
material_facts: The landlord and his family occupied the first floor of the building as their residence, while the tenant used the ground floor for banking business.
The landlord sought the ground floor as additional accommodation for residential use, relying on his and his wife's difficulty climbing stairs and the family's increased accommodation needs.
The lower courts had found the landlord's requirement bona fide and reasonable and had found comparative hardship in his favour.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was wrong to hold that the landlord could not seek residential accommodation under Section 10(3)(c) from a tenant occupying the remaining part for non-residential use.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10(3)(c) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1960 permits a landlord occupying part of a building to seek additional accommodation for residential purposes from a tenant occupying the whole or part of the remainder, even where that tenant uses it for non-residential purposes. The claim requires bona fide need and that the advantage to the landlord outweigh the hardship to the tenant. The Court relied on Sri Balaganesan Metals v. M.N. Shanmugham Chetty and Ors.

rule.if: additional_accommodation_eviction_proceeding and landlord_occupies_part_residentially and tenant_occupies_remaining_part_non_residentially and bona_fide_residential_need and landlord_advantage_outweighs_tenant_hardship

predicates.additional_accommodation_eviction_procee: A landlord seeks eviction to obtain additional accommodation in a building of which the landlord already occupies part.
predicates.landlord_occupies_part_residentially: The landlord occupies part of the building for residential purposes.
predicates.tenant_occupies_remaining_part_non_resid: The tenant occupies another part of the building and uses it for non-residential purposes.
predicates.bona_fide_residential_need: The landlord has a bona fide need for additional accommodation for residential purposes.
predicates.landlord_advantage_outweighs_tenant_hard: The advantage to the landlord from eviction outweighs the hardship to the tenant.

issues.definition: A landlord occupying part of a building residentially may seek a non-residentially used part occupied by a tenant for additional residential accommodation when the landlord's need is bona fide and the balance of advantage favours the landlord.

issues.legal_issue: The death of a landlord during eviction proceedings does not necessarily substantially diminish the family's need for the premises when the family need continues.
material_facts: The landlord died after the High Court's order, while the matter was proceeding on appeal.
The eviction claim also rested on the increasing accommodation needs of the landlord's family.
The landlord's married sons and their families, as well as his wife, remained beneficiaries of the proceedings, and the family had grown during the litigation.
issues.conclusion: The landlord's death did not substantially diminish the accommodation need in this case because the enlarged family and surviving beneficiaries continued to need the premises.
issues.legal_principle: Courts should take subsequent events into account cautiously. The effect of a landlord's death depends on whether the underlying need survives; a death does not substantially alter the need where the claim also rests on continuing family requirements and the family beneficiaries remain.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding and landlord_dies_during_proceedings and family_need_supports_claim and family_beneficiaries_remain

predicates.eviction_proceeding: A landlord seeks eviction of a tenant and the proceeding remains unresolved.
predicates.landlord_dies_during_proceedings: The landlord dies while the eviction proceeding is pending.
predicates.family_need_supports_claim: The claimed need for the premises includes the accommodation needs of the landlord's family.
predicates.family_beneficiaries_remain: Family members who benefit from the claimed accommodation need remain after the landlord's death.

issues.definition: When a landlord dies during an eviction proceeding but the family's accommodation need and the family beneficiaries remain, the death does not substantially diminish that need.
